mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure matches where Team A's shots FOR (recent window) is elevated relative to its all-prior baseline, and simultaneously assess whether shots_on_target FOR tracks proportionally or lags. Condition corner-kick FOR output on this joint shots/accuracy state rather than on either observable independently.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shot volume rises sharply but on-target ratio does not rise proportionally, corner-kick generation rises with shot volume — suggesting wide/blocked attempts rather than on-target pressure drive corners; the relationship between shots and corners is stronger in the high-volume/low-accuracy regime than in the high-volume/high-accuracy regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume surge in recent matches (shots FOR) co-occurs with a divergence in shot-conversion efficiency (shots_on_target FOR as a share of shots FOR), and this joint relationship — high recent shot volume paired with a stable or declining on-target ratio — conditions corner-kick generation differently than either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint conditioning on two distinct observables (shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR) simultaneously to characterise a ratio/accuracy dimension, then linking that joint state to a third observable (corners). No single-observable mirror or single-band split captures the interaction between volume and accuracy.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Construct a joint state variable: Team A's corners FOR (recent vs. all-prior) crossed with Team B's corners AGAINST (recent vs. all-prior). Measure total corner output in matches where both sides of the interaction are simultaneously elevated versus matches where only one or neither is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corner output rises more when both Team A's corners-for tendency and Team B's corners-against tendency are simultaneously above their respective baselines than when only one is elevated — indicating a super-additive joint effect rather than a simple sum of two independent single-observable signals.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corners-against rate has spiked sharply in recent matches relative to its all-prior baseline, while Team A's corners-for rate has also risen recently. The joint interaction between Team A's attacking corner-generation tendency and Team B's recent defensive corner-concession tendency — assessed together rather than as two independent mirrors — conditions the total corner output of the match.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship: Team A's FOR observable interacts with Team B's AGAINST observable for the same metric. The engine's covered class handles each mirror independently; it does not measure the interaction term between the two sides' divergences from baseline simultaneously.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure the cross-team half-level interaction: Team A's first-half goals FOR rate versus its second-half rate, crossed with Team B's first-half goals AGAINST rate versus its second-half rate. Condition first-half vs. second-half goal output on this joint asymmetry rather than on either team's half split alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: First-half goal output is elevated relative to second-half goal output when Team A's first-half scoring tendency and Team B's first-half defensive vulnerability are simultaneously above their respective second-half levels — the joint asymmetry amplifies the half-level skew beyond what either team's individual half split would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals are distributed asymmetrically across halves (first-half goals FOR substantially higher than second-half goals FOR relative to competition norms), while Team B concedes more in the first half than the second half. The joint half-level scoring/conceding asymmetry between the two teams — not just each team's own half split — conditions whether first-half goal output diverges from second-half goal output in this specific matchup.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct half-level observables from different teams (Team A's FOR half split and Team B's AGAINST half split), creating a cross-team, cross-half interaction. The covered class handles within-half splits for a single team but not the joint interaction across teams.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Identify matches where Team A holds possession substantially above 50% AND Team B's fouls FOR rate is elevated relative to competition baseline. Within this joint state, measure Team B's yellow card accumulation rate versus matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's yellow card rate rises when Team A's possession dominance and Team B's foul-committing tendency are jointly elevated — the combination of being chased/dispossessed frequently and committing fouls at a high rate produces more card accumulation than either dimension alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession dominance (well above 50% both all-prior and recently) combined with Team B's foul rate FOR (Team B commits more fouls than it draws) creates a joint possession-vs-foul-asymmetry state. This joint state — high possession for one team paired with high foul-committing tendency for the other — conditions yellow card accumulation differently than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables from different teams (possession FOR for Team A, fouls FOR for Team B) jointly conditioning a third observable (yellow cards FOR for Team B). This is a cross-team, multi-observable interaction not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Measure the ratio of Team B's shots-against to shots-on-target-against across historical windows (recent vs. all-prior). When this ratio widens (more total shots conceded but not proportionally more on-target), assess whether Team A's goal output and corner output are jointly elevated or whether the volume signal is misleading about actual threat quality.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's shots-against volume rises sharply but shots-on-target-against does not rise proportionally, Team A's corner generation rises with shot volume but goal conversion does not rise proportionally — indicating the shot-volume spike reflects lower-quality wide attempts rather than genuine on-target pressure, and the corner-to-goal conversion relationship saturates.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-against rate has spiked sharply in recent matches (nearly 20 shots against per game recently vs. ~12 all-prior), while Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST has remained relatively stable. This divergence between total shots allowed and on-target shots allowed — a widening gap suggesting more low-quality attempts being conceded — conditions whether Team A's corner-kick and shot volume translates into goals differently than the raw shot-volume signal alone would imply.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires jointly tracking two opponent-side observables (shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST for Team B) to derive a quality-vs-volume divergence, then linking that joint state to Team A's output observables (goals and corners). This is a multi-observable, cross-metric interaction not reducible to any single observable mirror or band.
